correctness.rationale: Every J_{3/2} positive root solves tan b=b in its unique (n*pi,(n+1/2)*pi) interval. An exact arctan phase formula, elementary sin/cos inequalities and b>pi yield 2<((n+1/2)pi)^2-b^2<2+1/pi^2. Congruence of three odd squares mod 8 proves an all-index squared-zero gap >Delta. Trig addition proves pair-sum Sidon and no positive root sum. Fourier transform of the unit three-ball and polarization convert the gap into the stated uniform dot-product bound at each vertex. The code checks only finite sanity examples.

value.rationale: Three mutually orthogonal exponentials form the smallest nontrivial ball-frequency triangle. Distances are constrained by Fourier zeros, but triangle inequalities alone do not exclude right angles or collinearity. Uniform nonzero dot-product separation across all radii and forbidden degeneracy provide a genuinely structural exact geometric restriction, directly related to recent ball exponential-basis questions.
